summary: The Waghai belt's secret — a forceful monsoon fall past Dungarda village, where a local guide is essential and the forest department posts warnings.
description:
Bhigu Dhodh, the waterfall at Koshmal village, is what Gira Falls was before the parking lot: a serious monsoon cascade twenty kilometres from Waghai that almost nobody outside the surrounding villages visits. The route runs from Waghai toward Bhenskatri on SH-171, right after the river bridge at Dungarda, then uphill twenty minutes to a village with no tourist setup whatsoever.

From the road it is about a thirty-minute walk to the falls — and despite a visible trail, first-timers reliably lose it, which is why a local guide is not a nicety but a requirement. The forest department has posted warning signage after past incidents; the rocks and the flow deserve the caution. One practical trap: mainstream maps place the village wrong — search for 'Kusmal' and confirm with people, not pins.

July to September is the window. Expect a proper drenching-green Dang experience, carried entirely on your own supplies and judgement.
highlights: Forceful monsoon fall with near-zero footfall
Twenty minutes uphill past Dungarda, then a 30-min walk
Local guide essential — the trail misleads first-timers
Forest-department warnings mark the real risk

modes.road: From Waghai toward Bhenskatri on SH-171; turn right after the Dungarda river bridge and climb ~20 minutes to Koshmal village
modes.rail: Waghai narrow gauge; Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: ~30-minute walk from the road; clear-looking trail that still needs a local guide
access.road_condition: Tarred to Dungarda, rough village climb after; slow in rain

visit.notes: Unmanaged site; forest-department warning boards apply — daylight only.

seasonality.notes: July–September only; the fall and the greenery both leave with the rains.

experience.photography_notes: Full-flow frames from the trail's last bend; protect gear — spray zone is wide in August.

amenities.guides: Hire in Koshmal village — essential, not optional

warnings: Heed the forest-department warning boards — there have been incidents here
Do not enter the flow or cross wet rock shelves
Go in a group with a village guide and daylight margin

tips: Maps mislead here — search 'Kusmal' and then trust people over pins
Combine with Gira Falls for a tame-vs-wild waterfall double
Kilad campsite makes the natural overnight base

faqs.q: Why do I need a guide if there's a trail?
faqs.a: The trail looks obvious and still loses first-timers — and the forest department's warnings exist because of past incidents. A village guide costs little and removes both problems.
